subject: Model routing for PCI tokenization — request for single-variant binding
messages:
From: Andrew Ng <andrew.ng@helixpay.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@helixpay.com, security@helixpay.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model routing for PCI tokenization — request for single-variant binding

Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. After our internal review the payments team at Helix wants to proceed with Redwood for the tokenization path, but with two strict requirements we need to bake into the integration:

1) All PCI tokenization calls must be pinned to the same model variant (no automatic fallback or model substitution).
2) The inference traffic must remain in the us-east-1 region (data residency + audit requirements).

We recognize this is an operational constraint, so we're asking for an exception from the default fallback policy and any cross-region routing. This will be part of our security attestation and will be included in the MAA/SLA.

I've attached the draft SLA and a short blurb for the security questionnaire (Helix_PCI_SLA.pdf, Helix_MAA_draft.docx). Can your team confirm feasibility (latency/SLO impacts and availability tradeoffs) and an ops plan we can include in our audit package? Helix is aiming to go live in Q3; we'd like confirmation within three business days if possible.

Appreciate it —
Andrew Ng
Senior Product Manager, Helix Pay
andrew.ng@helixpay.com

—— Attachment stubs: Helix_PCI_SLA.pdf (6 pages), Helix_MAA_draft.docx (editable)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: andrew.ng@helixpay.com, contracts@helixpay.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model routing for PCI tokenization — request for single-variant binding

Marcus / Lauren —

Looping you both in on Helix Pay's request. TL;DR: they want a hard bind to a single model variant (no fallback) + strict us-east-1 residency for all tokenization calls. They need an ops-runbook and feasibility notes for audits within 3 business days.

Key asks for engineering/product:
- Confirm whether we can enforce a no-fallback binding at the routing layer for a specific customer route.
- Enumerate availability risk and suggested mitigation (dedicated capacity, reserved pool, active-passive fallback to a pre-approved identical-quantized variant only under controlled maintenance windows).
- Provide expected p50/p95 latency delta if we enable strict single-variant binding vs. normal multi-variant routing.
- Outline what telemetry/logging we can produce for their auditors (request traces, model hashes, region tags).

Marcus — can you take the technical lead here and include an ops/rollback playbook and a recommended configuration? If we need a SLA exception (lower availability target or guaranteed dedicated capacity), call that out.

I'll handle contracting and push for the language that allows a pre-authorized maintenance fallback window (if engineering needs it). Helix is a named account; this is a priority.

Thanks —
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: andrew.ng@helixpay.com, security@helixpay.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model routing for PCI tokenization — request for single-variant binding

Sergio / Lauren / Andrew —

I've looked through the attachments and sketched a technical note. Short answer: feasible, with operational tradeoffs. Details below.

Feasibility notes:
- Enforcing single-variant binding: We can implement a routing rule that pins a customer route to an exact model id+artifact hash. That prevents automatic variant substitution. Implementation: small router change + metadata on route.
- No-fallback risk: This removes our ability to transparently route around degraded nodes/variants. If the pinned variant is unhealthy, requests will fail unless we provision another identical variant.

Mitigations we propose:
1) Dedicated reserved capacity: provision a small reserved pool (N GPUs) for Helix's route in us-east-1. If the pool is strictly reserved and the model artifacts are pre-warmed, fail rates should be minimal.
2) Synchronized active standby: keep an identical quantized variant in warm-standby in the same region — this preserves "single-variant identity" from a hash perspective if we can guarantee identical build artifacts and quantization pipeline. Requires an authenticated artifact promotion process.
3) Maintenance escape hatch: we can agree to a documented maintenance window where we allow a pre-approved fallback variant (signed off by Helix + Redwood legal). This keeps auditors happy and gives us an operational safety valve.

Latency impact:
- p50 negligibly different if artifacts are warm.
- p95 may increase by ~10-30ms under heavy load if there is contention on the reserved pool (we'll provide profiling numbers once we size).

Telemetry we can provide:
- Per-request model hash, node id, region, and routing decision trace (JSON lines).
- Aggregated availability and per-minute failure counts for the route.
- Audit log export (S3) with signed manifests for artifact hashes.

Next steps I recommend (fast track):
- Product/Contracts: sign off on maintenance escape window and explicit SLA language around availability & reserved capacity costs.
- Infra/Infra Ops: I'll draft a runbook (prewarm, artifact promotion, failover checklist) and estimate GPU hours needed.

I can have a first-pass runbook + capacity estimate by EOD tomorrow if we prioritize.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Marcus wants to attach a quick ops checklist but will follow up separately.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: andrew.ng@helixpay.com, contracts@helixpay.com, security@helixpay.com
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model routing for PCI tokenization — request for single-variant binding

Thanks Marcus — this aligns with what I expected. High-level guidance:

1) Prioritize rapid delivery: Marcus, please produce the ops-runbook and a blunt capacity estimate (GPU-hours and cost delta) by EOD tomorrow. Sergio, coordinate with contracts to get the maintenance escape language ready to attach to their MAA.

2) Canary plan: we will run an initial canary with a single Helix tenant on a reserved pool for 48 hours with elevated monitoring (on-call from infra + SRE). If canary looks clean, expand to full production.

3) Legal/Contracts: I want explicit sign-off on: (a) agreed maintenance windows; (b) what constitutes an "approved fallback"; (c) cost responsibility for reserved capacity. Sergio — loop in Legal and mark this as high priority.

I'll escalate to me if anything blocks go/no-go for the canary. Good work — let's move quickly.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
